typography_visual_philosophy.statement: Typography behaves as a layered identity landscape: a custom white mountain/stone-like title object occupies the photographic field while orange path, badge, handwritten voice, repeated claim rhythm, quiet functional copy, and footer lockup establish ordered reads.

stable_typography_grammar.statement: A newly approved display-lettering asset forms an irregular landscape-like central silhouette through unequal glyph mass, carved negative space and controlled erosion without copying source glyphs.
Repeated compact claims, restrained support copy, handwritten voice and footer identity establish distinct first/second/third reads around the display mass.
A restrained accent path links title and badge while a related accent voice appears in the handwritten slogan; it is semantic connection, not generic decoration.
High-contrast display and quieter support layers remain spatially legible against a deep photographic environment without isolating typography in a separate panel.

variation_axes_typography.statement: Claim count and exact claim wording may change if repeated upper cadence and hierarchy remain truthful.
Accent hue and path shape may adapt when the accent remains limited, semantically connected, and secondary to the display title.
Photographic subject may change if it provides complex dark spatial texture and preserves display/support contrast roles.

production_bound_typography.transfer_behavior: RECOMPOSE; DO_NOT TREAT AS FAMILY INVARIANTS

typography_content_compatibility.statement: A transfer needs a short locked display name that can sustain a newly authored silhouette plus enough truthful support copy for at least two subordinate reads.
A high-complexity photographic field must leave a legible central occupancy zone and sufficient top/bottom separation for functional text.

renderer_responsibility: photographic background and complex pixel art
display-lettering exploration only through an authorized source-pipeline route
figma_responsibility: exact functional Chinese and English live text
placement of approved display-title or handwritten assets

transfer_risks: stock-font substitution would remove the central landscape silhouette
literal copying of source glyphs or WANCE identity would leak brand-bound content
decorative English filler would corrupt the claim hierarchy
an orange underline or generic seal would collapse the semantic accent system
a bright or flat background could destroy the evidence-backed text-image contrast
